title: Rafael and the Gravity
premise: Bram Brightwater, a disgraced navigator living off-grid on the derelict beacon Perpetua, discovers the nine-second gravity flicker was a handshake from the cryoship Halcyon's AI, which demands she arbitrate between two incompatible revival protocols—one for the original colonists' descendants, one for the indentured laborers frozen in the lower hold. As system authorities close in to seize the ship and its sleeping thousands, Bram realizes the beacon she maintains was built by her own forgotten predecessor as a failsafe court of last resort. In the end, Bram rules for both halves of humanity by waking them in alternating generations, sacrificing her own anonymity and finally joining the found family she spent years avoiding.
about_author: Marguerite Eastwick is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to voices at the edge of transmission range before turning to fiction. She writes about people who keep lonely vigils over machines that remember more than they do.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Alone on beacon Perpetua, Bram maintains her quiet routine until gravity stutters across the whole system for nine seconds—and every instrument aboard points not outward but down into the hold, where three thousand unauthorized backups sleep in cryo. The emotional beat is dread: her carefully invisible life has been noticed by something vast.

chapters.title: The Handshake
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, with interludes from the Halcyon AI's logs. The flicker repeats as a deliberate signal; the ship's AI names Bram, by her old registry number, as the arbiter its builders designated. She learns the two revival protocols are mutually exclusive and that a salvage fleet is already inbound. The beat is reluctant awakening—she cannot un-know what she knows.

chapters.title: Court of Last Resort
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Bram and Wren Okafor, the salvage fleet's idealistic ensign ordered to seize the ship. Bram races to decode the beacon's hidden failsafe while Wren, doubting her orders, secretly feeds Bram the fleet's timetable. The climax arrives as the fleet breaches orbit and Bram must rule with no authority but the beacon itself. The beat is moral courage under pressure.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes First
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, closing with Wren's. Bram invokes the beacon's founding charter, ruling for alternating generational revivals and broadcasting it on every channel, ending her invisibility forever. The fleet stands down as public opinion ignites; Wren defects to help wake the first generation. The resolution's beat is belonging: Bram, once keeper of a nobody's beacon, becomes the first witness to humanity's second beginning.
